reply_text:
I found one 2026 candidate, and I only saw it in news coverage, not in Legg's own words. On 16 September 2026 he launched the DeepMind Institute. Reuters, summarising a Financial Times interview I couldn't open, reported that he remained "comfortable" with his forecast of a 50% chance of "minimal" AGI by 2028. Only those two quoted words are presented as his. The rest is Reuters' paraphrase of the FT, and the forecast itself is an old one he said he still holds.

- **His own 2026 writing:** the institute's launch essay (16 September, signed by Legg, James Manyika and Demis Hassabis) gives no date. It says "we expect those gaps to be closed soon", meaning the gaps between today's AI and full AGI. I've listed it under undated.
- **No dated claims:** the 29 October economics essay he co-wrote contains no dated prediction about AI.
- **Other years:** the podcast interviews that state the 2028 forecast are from 2025 (Google DeepMind podcast, 11 December 2025) and 2023 (Dwarkesh Patel). Two secondary sites seem to treat that 2025 podcast as a 2026 statement. That includes AIMultiple's line about a "January 2026" prediction, which wasn't in the page text I fetched.
- **Gaps:** I didn't open his 16 September X post or the FT article itself. His Auckland lecture, "AGI Incoming", is set for 4 December 2026 and hasn't happened yet. I used 9 of 12 searches and all 6 page openings. One opening went to the institute's homepage, which has no prediction on it.
